levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A conclusion is stated with no figures behind it.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Figures are quoted but the step from figure to conclusion is missing.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response shows which figures drive the conclusion and how.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response also says how large a change in a figure would flip the conclusion.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The method from the earlier case is restated without being applied.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The method is applied but a difference in the new case is ignored.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The method is applied and adjusted for what is different in the new case.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The method is applied, adjusted, and the limit of the transfer is stated.

judgment.prompt: Lachlan’s side business brought in $21,800 and his tax rose by more than the income tax on it alone. Explain what the self-employment contribution adds, and say what a person starting a side business should set aside from each payment received.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that the net $15,400.00 attracts both income tax and the 14.2% self-employment contribution, while employment income of the same size would attract only the income tax in this schedule.
Gives usable advice grounded in the figures: setting aside roughly 28% of net self-employment income covers both the 14% income tax band and the 14.2% contribution.
Notes that nothing is withheld, so the amount has to be set aside deliberately and paid in instalments of $546.70.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the $2,186.80 self-employment contribution and the $4,956.00 income tax.
lookFors: The set-aside percentage is derived from the two rates rather than guessed.
The response distinguishes revenue from net income when describing what to set aside.
A response noting that expenses reduce both charges is reading the structure correctly.
judgment.commonMisconception: Assuming self-employment income is taxed in the same way as employment income.

judgment.prompt: Taxable income came to $38,200.00, just under the $38,400 threshold. Say what would happen to the tax on the next $1,000 of self-employment profit, and why the answer is not simply 14%.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: States that $200 of the next $1,000 stays in the 14% band and $800 falls into the 22% band, giving $204 of income tax rather than $140.
Adds that the same $1,000 also attracts the 14.2% self-employment contribution, so the total on it is about $346.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $38,200.00 taxable income and the $38,400 threshold in the calculation.
lookFors: The response splits the $1,000 across the two bands rather than applying one rate.
The self-employment contribution is included in the total.
judgment.commonMisconception: Applying a single marginal rate to income that straddles a threshold.
